name: Myllymatti
description: Myllymatti is a Finnish card game that is the ancestor of the Swedish game Skitgubbe and the Norwegian game Mattis. It is a two-phase game: first players collect cards by winning tricks, then they try to get rid of those cards by beating opponents' cards. The last player holding cards loses.

overview.description: Myllymatti is a Finnish card game that is the ancestor of the Swedish game Skitgubbe and the Norwegian game Mattis. It is a two-phase game: first players collect cards by winning tricks, then they try to get rid of those cards by beating opponents' cards. The last player holding cards loses.

history.origins: Myllymatti originated in Finland and is mentioned in several 19th century newspaper articles. It is the direct ancestor of Swedish Skitgubbe (also known as Mas or Mjolnarmatte) and Norwegian Mattis.
timeline: 19th Century: Mentioned in Finnish newspaper articles as a popular game
Early 20th Century: Spreads to Sweden as Skitgubbe
Mid 20th Century: Norwegian variant Mattis develops
history.cultural: Part of the Nordic card game tradition. The Finnish origin makes it historically significant as the source of a game family played across Scandinavia.
history.evolution: The game spread from Finland to Sweden and Norway, with each country developing slight variations while maintaining the core two-phase mechanic.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ranking: A (high), K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (low).
setup.dealing: All cards dealt evenly - 17 cards to each player, with one card set aside or dealer takes the extra.

rules.objective: Avoid being the last player holding cards after both phases.
rules.gameplay: Phase one: only two players play to each trick. Player to dealer's left begins with the next player clockwise; higher card wins. If the leader wins, the same two continue; if the second player wins, they start with the next player. Phase two: single cards only. Play a card that beats the previous (suit rank Spades > Hearts > Diamonds > Clubs) or pick up the previous card; then the next player leads. Last player holding cards loses.
keyRules: Phase One: Win tricks to collect cards
Phase Two: Beat cards or pick them up
Suit ranking in Phase Two: Spades > Hearts > Diamonds > Clubs

strategy.basic: In Phase One, try to win tricks to collect high cards for Phase Two, but do not collect too many cards. In Phase Two, save your highest cards for when you really need them.
strategy.intermediate: In Phase One, control when you win tricks - winning early tricks gives you control but also more cards to shed later. Try to collect cards in strong suits (Spades and Hearts).
strategy.advanced: Card counting is crucial. Track which high cards have been played in Phase One to predict opponents' holdings in Phase Two. In Phase Two, force opponents to use their high cards early by playing medium cards that are difficult to beat without using premium cards.
tips: Do not win too many tricks in Phase One - each card won is a card you must shed in Phase Two
Save Aces and Kings of Spades for critical moments in Phase Two
Try to maintain cards in multiple suits to have flexibility in Phase Two
If you have many low cards, consider picking up early in Phase Two to consolidate your hand

scoring.description: No scoring - the loser is simply the last player holding cards.
scoring.winCondition: Be the first to play all your cards in Phase Two. Avoid being the last player holding cards.
